# ============================================================================
# OPEN ANALYTICS WORK: PIECE TEMPLATE. Do not edit this file; COPY it:
#
#   cp content/open-analytics/_post-template.md content/open-analytics/<slug>.md
#
# Slug = file name: lowercase, hyphens only, descriptive, no dates, no underscores.
# Files starting with "_" are never built. Fill every field, delete these
# comments, then run:   python3 scripts/open_analytics.py
#
# INTEGRITY: only Brandon's real analysis goes here.
# Agents may edit structure, wording and formatting, but must never invent
# data, figures, findings, sources or methods.
#
# FIELDS
#   title        Specific and descriptive; put the useful words first.
#   description  70–160 chars. The search snippet. Names the subject and the payoff.
#   question     The question this analysis answers, phrased as a question.
#   summary      The answer in 1–2 plain sentences (≤ 60 words). Answer engines
#                quote this, so it must stand alone, out of context.
#   date         YYYY-MM-DD. A future date is not published until that day's build.
#   updated      Optional YYYY-MM-DD, when findings or data change.
#   tags         2–4 from content/site.json → sections.openAnalytics.tags.
#   data         Plain description of the data source(s).
#   data_url     Optional public link to the dataset (adds Dataset JSON-LD).
#   methods      One line: how the analysis was done.
#   tools        Optional list, e.g. [Python, pandas, Looker Studio].
#   repo_url     Optional link to code or notebook.
#   status       Optional: complete | ongoing | superseded.
#   canonical    Optional. ONLY for a cross-post whose original lives elsewhere
#                (e.g. on rogue0015.github.io). Points search engines to it and
#                keeps this copy out of the sitemap.
#   draft        true to keep it unpublished.
#
# BODY RULES
#   1. Start with "## Key findings" as a bullet list (3–5 bullets; each one a
#      complete, self-contained finding with its number and unit).
#   2. Then explain: context, data, method, results, limits, what to do with it.
#   3. Tables: GitHub pipe tables; add "Table: caption" on the line after.
#   4. Charts: real images with alt text that states the finding, not "chart".
#   5. Always include a "## Limits" section: sample, bias, missing data.
# ============================================================================
title: "A clear, specific title for the analysis"
description: "A concise summary that names the subject and why the finding matters to the reader."
question: "What question does this analysis answer?"
summary: "One or two sentences that state the main finding plainly."
date: 2026-01-01
tags: [data, zimbabwe]
data: "Where the data came from, when it was collected, and how much of it there is"
data_url: ""
methods: "How the analysis was done, in one line"
tools: [Python]
repo_url: ""
status: complete
draft: true
---
